name: Jakobskreuz Buchensteinwand
kurzbeschreibung: The Jakobskreuz (Jacob's Cross) on the 1,456 m high Buchensteinwand in the Pillersee Valley: at 30 m tall, it's the world's largest walkable summit cross with four viewing platforms.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Jakobskreuz (Jacob's Cross) towers on the 1,456-meter-high summit of the Buchensteinwand in Tyrol's Pillersee Valley (Kitzbühel district), forming a widely visible architectural landmark of the Kitzbühel Alps. With a total height of almost 30 meters, this imposing double cross is the world's largest walkable summit cross. Erected in honor of Saint James – the patron saint of the traditional pilgrimage route Jakobsweg Tirol, which passes through the valley – the monument combines spiritual pilgrimage tradition with state-of-the-art wood and steel construction architecture. From its four cantilevered viewing arms, a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic view opens up over the Kitzbühel mountains, the snow-capped Hohe Tauern, and the rugged limestone massifs of the Wilder Kaiser, as well as the Loferer and Leoganger Steinberge.

Route & Requirements

The Buchensteinwand is a popular excursion destination for families and hikers of all ages. The most comfortable way to reach the Jakobskreuz is by taking the 4-seater chairlift of the Bergbahn Pillersee, which starts in St. Jakob in Haus and transports guests directly to the summit in about 12 minutes. For those who prefer to hike, there are well-marked trails leading up to the summit, offering varying degrees of difficulty. The ascent on foot typically takes around 1.5 to 2 hours, depending on the chosen route and individual fitness level. The trails are generally well-maintained and suitable for regular hikers.

Visit & Arrival

The Jakobskreuz is open daily from 09:00 to 16:45 during the summer and winter seasons of the Bergbahnen Pillersee (summer operation usually from mid-May to the end of October). Admission to the Jakobskreuz is available either separately or as a discounted combi-ticket with the mountain railway. Fares for a round trip including Jakobskreuz admission (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €29.00, Seniors approx. €26.00, Children (born 2009–2018) approx. €15.00; pure admission to the cross (for hikers) approx. €9.50. Significant discounts apply with the regional PillerseeTal Card or the Kitzbüheler Alpen Summer Card. By car, you can reach the valley station of the Bergbahn Pillersee via the B164 to Fieberbrunn or St. Jakob in Haus, where ample parking is available.

Tips

Thanks to the modern chairlift and the integrated passenger elevator inside the cross, the entire Jakobskreuz is completely barrier-free and wheelchair-accessible for visitors with limited mobility and families with strollers. Directly at the foot of the cross, the Berggasthof Buchensteinwand mountain inn with its large sun terrace invites you to enjoy Tyrolean delicacies. Visit the cross in the morning on a clear day to capture the rugged peaks of the Loferer Steinberge in perfect photographic light. Plan enough time to explore the various viewing platforms and the changing exhibitions in the arms of the cross. A stroll along the family-friendly Blumen- und Sagenweg Buchensteinwand (Flower and Legend Trail) around the cross completes the visit.
